settings.question: Where are your shops?
settings.answer: We have two Calgary shops: 111 42 Ave SW (our main location, (403) 452-4283) and Unit 101, 3928 Edmonton Trail NE ((825) 395-4024). See both locations.

settings.question: What are your hours?
settings.answer:
42 Ave SW: [[hours_sw]]

Edmonton Trail NE: [[hours_ne]]

Both shops close over the Friday midday break.

settings.question: Do I need an appointment, or can I walk in?
settings.answer: Walk-ins are welcome and are fitted around booked work. Booked appointments are served first, so requesting a time online is the fastest way in.

settings.question: Is my online booking confirmed right away?
settings.answer: No. An online booking is a request until our staff confirm it. We confirm by text or phone before your visit.

settings.question: How long does a tire installation take?
settings.answer: Tire installation takes about 45–60 minutes. A seasonal changeover or rotation takes about 30 minutes, balancing about 20 minutes, and a flat repair 20–30 minutes.

settings.question: Which shop does road force balancing?
settings.answer: Road force balancing is done only at our Edmonton Trail NE shop. Regular wheel balancing is available at both shops.

settings.question: What areas do you serve?
settings.answer: We serve drivers across Calgary: NE, NW, SE and SW. All work is done at our two shops; we do not offer mobile tire service.

settings.question: How much is tire installation?
settings.answer: From $30 per tire. Installation includes mounting, computer balancing, a new valve stem, TPMS inspection and reset, and torque to the manufacturer's spec. Tires bought elsewhere, including online, are installed at $30 per tire for a car or SUV and $35 for a truck. Details on tire installation.

settings.question: Do you offer free installation?
settings.answer: No. Installation is from $30 per tire, and balancing is included in that price.

settings.question: How much is a seasonal tire swap?
settings.answer: If your other set is already on its own rims, it is $15 per tire for cars, SUVs, vans and EVs ($60 for four) and $20 per tire for trucks. A trailer is $100 flat. If both sets share one set of rims, each tire has to be dismounted and rebalanced, so that is priced as tire installation. See seasonal changeover.

settings.question: How much is a tire rotation?
settings.answer: $15 per tire for cars, SUVs, vans and EVs ($60 for four). $20 per tire for pickups, heavy-duty trucks and duallys, for the whole set. See tire rotation.

settings.question: How much is wheel balancing?
settings.answer: Wheel balancing is $20 per wheel ($80 for four). Road force balancing, at our Edmonton Trail NE shop only, is $35 per wheel ($140 for four), or $20 per tire when added to another job there. See road force balancing.

settings.question: How much does a flat tire repair cost?
settings.answer: $50 per tire. We do a permanent internal patch-plug with the tire off the rim, warrantied for the life of the tire. We do not do external plugs as a repair. See flat tire repair.

settings.question: Can every flat tire be repaired?
settings.answer: No. Punctures in the sidewall or shoulder, holes larger than about 6 mm, a spot that has already been repaired, or a tire that was driven flat cannot be safely repaired. In those cases the tire needs to be replaced.

settings.question: Are there extra fees on new tires?
settings.answer: Alberta charges a tire recycling levy of about $5 per new tire sold; it is a provincial fee shown separately. Leaving your old tires with us is included when you buy new tires from us. If you bring your own tires, disposal of the old ones is an optional $5 per tire.

settings.question: Is a re-torque included?
settings.answer: Yes. A re-torque at 50–100 km after any wheel is removed is free.

settings.question: Do you price match?
settings.answer: Yes. We match the tire price on a written quote from a local independent tire shop in Calgary, for the same tire. We do not match chains or online stores, and quotes older than 30 days don't count. Installation, balancing, the tire levy and other fees are charged at our normal prices. Full rules on our price match page.

settings.question: Do you offer road hazard protection?
settings.answer: Yes, as an optional paid add-on on any brand: 10% of the tire price ($12–$50 per tire), covering 12 months. It is not included automatically. See road hazard protection.

settings.question: Can I bring my own tires that I bought online?
settings.answer: Yes. We install tires bought elsewhere at the install-only rate: $30 per tire for a car or SUV, $35 for a truck.

settings.question: Which tire brands do you carry?
settings.answer: Michelin, Bridgestone, BFGoodrich, Toyo, Yokohama, Continental, Cooper, Firestone, General Tire, Kumho, Mickey Thompson, Falken, Nexen and Dunlop, with Pirelli, Hankook and Goodyear available in store. Browse all tires.

settings.question: Do you sell wheels and rims?
settings.answer: Yes, alloy wheels and steel winter rims, and winter tire packages on steel rims. See wheels and rims.

settings.question: Do you sell used tires?
settings.answer: No. We sell new tires only.

settings.question: Do you do wheel alignments?
settings.answer: No. We offer balancing and rotation, but we do not perform wheel alignments.

settings.question: Do you store tires?
settings.answer: No. We do not offer tire storage; your off-season set goes home with you.

settings.question: Do you work on trailers and trucks?
settings.answer: Yes. We sell ST-rated trailer tires (load ranges C to E) and complete trailer wheel assemblies, plus light truck tires in all-terrain, mud-terrain and highway-terrain. See trailer tires and light truck tires.

settings.question: Do you work with fleets and businesses?
settings.answer: Yes. Fleets and commercial customers get volume pricing; see fleet tires. Tire shops and dealers can apply for a trade account on our wholesale page.

settings.question: When should I put winter tires on in Calgary?
settings.answer: Once daily highs stay below 7°C, usually mid-to-late October. Winter tires outperform all-seasons below 7°C even before the first snow. They come off around April, on the same 7°C line.

settings.question: Are winter tires required by law in Alberta?
settings.answer: No. Alberta has no winter tire law. British Columbia requires them on Hwy 1 and Hwy 93 west of the Alberta border from October 1 to April 30.

settings.question: Are studded tires legal in Alberta?
settings.answer: Yes, year-round. We sell studded and studless winter tires; see studded tires.

settings.question: Do I need four winter tires or just two?
settings.answer: Four. Winter tires go on all four wheels, including on front-wheel drive cars. Mixing grip front to rear can make the rear slide out in corners.

settings.question: What payment methods do you accept?
settings.answer: We accept cash, debit and credit cards.

settings.question: Can I return tires?
settings.answer: Yes, if they have not been installed or mounted. Unused tires, wheels and accessories can be returned within 30 days of purchase for a refund to your original payment method, with your receipt. Once tires are installed or mounted the sale is final, except for defects covered by the manufacturer's warranty. Services already performed are not refundable. See our returns policy.

settings.question: How do I contact you?
settings.answer: Call the 42 Ave SW shop at (403) 452-4283, the Edmonton Trail NE shop at (825) 395-4024, or email info@princetires.ca.

settings.question: How much is TPMS sensor replacement?
settings.answer: $60 per sensor. Checking and resetting your TPMS is included with tire installation. See TPMS service.

settings.question: Do you do free tire inspections and pressure checks?
settings.answer: Yes. A tire inspection and a pressure check are free at both shops, and a re-torque at 50–100 km after any wheel is removed is free too. Just stop by.
